description: Mississippi-only rules checked against the Mississippi Department of Education driver-education document, which reprints the passenger-automobile speed table, the DUI concentration rules, and Mississippi Code §63-1-9. National rules stay in the baseline. No fines.

questions.q: The document states that the maximum speed for any vehicle in a school zone is
questions.explanation: The rules-of-the-road text says the maximum speed for any vehicle in a school zone is 15 mph. That sentence does not add a children-present or flashing-beacon condition, so this question does not add one.

provenance.manual: Mississippi Driver Education and Training Program Requirements

questions.q: The Natchez Trace Parkway speed in the passenger-automobile table is
questions.explanation: The table lists the Natchez Trace Parkway at 50 mph maximum. It is a separate line from the interstate, four-lane, and two-lane entries.

provenance.manual: Mississippi Driver Education and Training Program Requirements

questions.q: The document's under-the-influence statement treats a driver 21 or older as under the influence of intoxicating alcohol if the BAC registers
questions.explanation: The section headed 'How much is too much?' says a person 21 or older is under the influence of intoxicating alcohol if the BAC registers .08% or more.

provenance.manual: Mississippi Driver Education and Training Program Requirements

questions.q: For a driver under 21, that same statement uses a BAC of
options: .08 percent or more, the same as an adult
questions.explanation: The same statement says a person under the age of 21 is under the influence of intoxicating alcohol if the BAC registers .02% or more. A nearby heading also says Mississippi has zero tolerance for underage drivers under the influence of alcohol.

provenance.manual: Mississippi Driver Education and Training Program Requirements

questions.q: If a driver refuses the officer's request for a breath or chemical test, the document says the license is administratively suspended for
options: 45 days, which is only the length of the temporary receipt
questions.explanation: The refusal section says the officer's receipt is a temporary permit valid for 45 days, and the license will be administratively suspended for 90 days for refusing the breath or chemical test.

provenance.manual: Mississippi Driver Education and Training Program Requirements
provenance.section: Refusal of a breath or chemical test

questions.q: The reprinted license statute does not use a demerit-point total. Before a 16-year-old can qualify for a driver's license, a learner's permit must be held for at least one year
options: With no section 63-11-30 or moving-violation conviction
If the driver completes a point-reduction course
questions.explanation: The reprint of Mississippi Code §63-1-9(2)(b) requires that clean year. A conviction under section 63-11-30 or of a moving violation restarts the one-year requirement. The document does not publish a point schedule.

provenance.manual: Mississippi Code, reprinted in the Driver Education and Training Program Requirements

questions.q: A learner's permit may be issued to a person who is at least
questions.explanation: The reprinted §63-1-9(2)(a) says a learner's permit may be issued to any person who is at least 15 who otherwise meets the requirements of the article.

provenance.manual: Mississippi Code, reprinted in the Driver Education and Training Program Requirements

questions.q: The regular learner's permit described in the same document allows driving when accompanied by a licensed driver who is
options: 18 or older and seated anywhere in the vehicle
21 or older and seated next to the driver
questions.explanation: The regular-learner's-permit text says the permit entitles the holder to drive when accompanied by a licensed driver aged 21 or older who is physically occupying the seat next to the driver. It also says the permit is valid for two years.

provenance.manual: Mississippi Driver Education and Training Program Requirements

questions.q: A driver's license may be issued at 16 to a person who otherwise qualifies and who has held a learner's permit for at least one year without a disqualifying conviction. The reprinted statute also says an applicant
options: Who turns 17 before holding the learner's permit for one year is not eligible until the year ends
Who is 16+ with a six-month out-of-state license need not hold a Mississippi permit first
Must be 18 before any license is issued
Must log 50 hours in the statute itself
questions.explanation: The reprinted §63-1-9(2)(d) states that six-month out-of-state-license exception. The one-year permit rule for a 16-year-old applicant is in paragraph (b). Who is at least 16 and has held a valid license from another state for at least six months is not required to hold a Mississippi learner's permit first.

provenance.manual: Mississippi Code, reprinted in the Driver Education and Training Program Requirements

questions.q: Under the reprinted statute, a person under 18 who does not present a diploma, GED certificate, or the listed school-enrollment documentation
options: May receive a full driver's license after passing the road test
May not get a license or permit, subject to listed alternatives
Is limited to daytime driving only
May drive with a parent for 90 days without a permit
questions.explanation: The reprinted §63-1-9(1)(f) prohibits issuance to a person under 18 who does not present a diploma or GED, or for whom the department has not received documentation of the listed enrollment, home-school, or section 63-1-10 circumstances. May not be issued a driver's license or learner's permit, subject to the enrollment and hardship alternatives the section lists.

provenance.manual: Mississippi Code, reprinted in the Driver Education and Training Program Requirements

questions.q: In Mississippi, what is the youngest age at which you can get a learner's permit for a car?
questions.explanation: Mississippi issues a learner's permit for a car at 15 years at the earliest.

questions.q: In Mississippi, how long must a driver under 18 hold a learner's permit before moving to the next license?
questions.explanation: Mississippi requires drivers under 18 to hold the learner's permit for 12 months.

provenance.manual: Regular Learner's Permit | DPS Driver Service Bureau

questions.q: In Mississippi, what is the youngest age at which a teen can get a license to drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: In Mississippi, the earliest unsupervised (provisional) license is at 16 years.

questions.q: In Mississippi, what is the youngest age for a full, unrestricted car license?
questions.explanation: Mississippi drivers can hold an unrestricted license at 16½ years.

questions.q: How many questions are on the Mississippi car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: The Mississippi car knowledge test has 30 questions.

questions.q: What score do you need to pass the Mississippi car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: You need 80% to pass the Mississippi car knowledge test.

questions.q: In Mississippi, a driver 21 or older is legally impaired at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: In Mississippi, drivers 21 and older are over the limit at 0.08% or more.

questions.q: In Mississippi, a driver under 21 breaks the law at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: Mississippi sets the under-21 limit at 0.02%.

questions.q: In Mississippi, how long is the license suspension for an adult's first refusal of a breath or blood test?
questions.explanation: A first refusal in Mississippi brings a suspension of 90 days.

questions.q: What is the highest standard speed limit for cars on rural interstates in Mississippi?
questions.explanation: Rural interstates in Mississippi can be posted up to 70 mph for cars.

questions.q: Which best describes Mississippi's law on drivers using a phone?
options: Only texting is banned for all drivers
Phone use is banned only for new or young drivers
No statewide ban on phone use or texting
Hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers
questions.explanation: Mississippi: only texting is banned for all drivers.

questions.q: When is a left turn on a red light allowed in Mississippi?
options: From a one-way or two-way street onto a one-way street
Only from a one-way street onto a one-way street
questions.explanation: In Mississippi, a left turn on red (after a full stop, where not prohibited) is allowed: only from a one-way street onto a one-way street.

questions.q: How is Mississippi's seat belt law for adults enforced?
options: No seat belt law for adults
Primary: police can stop you just for not wearing a seat belt
Secondary: police can cite you only after stopping you for something else
questions.explanation: Mississippi seat belt enforcement is primary.

questions.q: Until what age must a child ride in a car seat or booster seat in Mississippi?
questions.explanation: Mississippi requires a car seat or booster until 7 years, with height or weight exceptions.

questions.q: What is Mississippi's minimum liability insurance (injury per person / injury per crash / property damage)?
questions.explanation: Mississippi requires at least $25,000 / $50,000 / $25,000.
